text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- A 45-member unit of the Estonian Defence Forces returned from the NATO exercise Cooperative Nugget in the United States.

- Reforms in the interior ministry and the police and changes already made in the structure and subordination system would make the work of these institutions more effective, Interior Minister Robert Lepikson said.
- An April survey on Estonians in Russian-dominated eastern Viru county showed that 70 percent of those questioned were satisfied with their economic situation.
- Lepikson said after a meeting with a representative of the Moscow Patriarchate on Friday that a compromise over a dispute between Orthodox branchs in Estonia was possible.
- The police are investigating the sale of nine vessels by the joint-stock company Ookean in 1995 in a criminal case against its former manager.
- The 36th Kalev moto-race was held on the Pirita track in Tallinn at the weekend.

- Defence Minister Andrus Oovel met his Polish counterpart Stanislav Dobrzanski in Warsaw on Sunday and was assured of Poland's support to Estonia's aims for full membership of NATO and the European Union and for the launch of a joint Baltic military academy.
- A renovated waste water purification plant will be opened today in Rapla. Only six out of 26 towns in Estonia with populations over 5,000 have satisfactory sewage and purification systems.
- Results of the first quarter of 1997 point to direct foreign investment in Estonia of 2.5 billion kroons by the end of the year without including investments into infrastructure.
